outcome: Stability of methylation patterns in circulating blood cells from birth to adolescence
cohort: 203 mother-newborn pairs from the PlaNS birth cohort and 808 participants from the ARIES database
finding: Neonatal sex and maternal pre-pregnancy BMI and gestational weight gain were associated with methylation of serotonin-regulating genes in cord blood cells, and these methylation patterns were stable from birth to adolescence.
